name: wheel_axle
title: A pair of wheels on a plate with two wheel pins, built into the bottom layer of a chassis.
why: Every small car, truck, or trailer stands on these; the wheels sit on pins, not on loose axles.

name: wheel_arch
title: A mudguard over a pair of wheels, so the body clears them and the arch shows round over each wheel.
why: A mudguard over each axle lets the body sit low with the wheels showing, the way town cars are built.

name: headlights
title: A vehicle's lights in its front face, headlight bricks with round clear tiles on their front studs.
why: Lights in the front face of a car or truck, recessed in headlight bricks.

name: tail_lights
title: Red lights in a vehicle's back face, on bricks with a stud on one side, with tiles flush between them.
why: A smooth back with red lights at its corners, all on studs that face backward.

name: windscreen
title: A sloped windscreen on a vehicle's cab, with a roof of tiles over it.
why: The sloped windscreen and roof of a car's or truck's cab.

name: curved_hood
title: A vehicle's hood that rounds down to the front, curved slopes on a plate.
why: A hood that rounds down to the front instead of ending in a step.

name: trailer_hitch
title: A tow ball under the back of a vehicle and a socket on a trailer's drawbar, so the trailer swings.
why: Lets a trailer or caravan swing behind the car that tows it.

name: front_bumper
title: A bumper that stands out across a vehicle's front, a plate under the front edge with a tile on top and round indicator lights at its ends.
why: A bumper that stands out from the front with indicator lights at its ends.

name: bracket_side_panel
title: A vehicle's smooth side, a panel of plate and tiles built lying flat and pressed onto brackets whose studs face out.
why: Smooth, flush sides on a vehicle: the truck book's most-used method.

name: cab_seat
title: A driver's seat with a steering wheel in front of it, on a cab's floor.
why: A driver's seat and steering wheel for any cab or car.

name: light_bar
title: A row of lamps along a vehicle's roof edge, round plates on a bracket whose face hangs over the edge.
why: Lamps along a roof's edge for emergency vehicles, buses, and trucks.

name: front_grille
title: A truck's grille, grille tiles on bricks whose studs face the front, between the headlights.
why: A truck's grille, smooth and ribbed, between its headlights.

name: tilting_hood
title: A hood on hinge bricks, so the whole nose of a vehicle tips up to show the engine.
why: A nose that tips up on hinges to show the engine, a favorite play feature.

name: spliced_chassis
title: A long chassis from two plates butted end to end, locked by plates across the seam.
why: A chassis longer than any single plate, locked across the joint so it doesn't bend.

name: rear_spoiler
title: A wing over the back of a car, a tile on a plate held up on two small posts.
why: A wing over the back of a sports or race car.

name: exhaust_stack
title: A truck's upright exhaust pipe beside its cab, round bricks on a bracket with a cone on top.
why: A truck's upright exhaust pipe beside the cab.

name: cargo_pallet
title: A pallet with slots underneath for a forklift's forks, with crates stacked on it.
why: Loads for trucks, forklifts, warehouses, and station platforms.

name: train_carriage
title: A 6-wide passenger carriage's body on a train base, window bands along both sides, doors at the ends, and a roof that curves down at its edges.
why: A passenger carriage for a train set, with window bands and a round roof.

name: hinged_tailgate
title: A truck bed's tailgate on hinge bricks, so it folds down.
why: A pickup's or trailer's tailgate that folds down.

name: technic_spine
title: A long, stiff beam of two rows of Technic bricks side by side, their joints offset, pinned together through their holes, so it can't bend at a joint.
why: A long beam that doesn't bend, under trailers, cranes, and long floors.
